corridor.line: Past the gate the passage runs straight, and then runs out of light.

inspect.say: The dust lies even from wall to wall and nothing has walked it. Halfway down, a band of flagstones sits a finger lower than the rest, and the dust has run off their edges into the seams. The stone on either side of the band is worn hollow, the way a step is worn by being taken.
The band of stone sits where it sat. The dust over it has not moved.

objects.name: the floor, under a skin of dust

look.say: The alcove is cut at shoulder height and it is empty. The stone at the back of it is black with smoke, and the black stops in a clean line, the way it does where something stood in front of it for a long time.

objects.name: an alcove cut in the wall

cross.say: You walk to where the light stops, and keep walking. The floor tilts down under you and goes on tilting. The cold coming up is the cold that was on the far side of the gate, and it has been standing here the whole while.

objects.name: the dark, where the corridor gives out

follow.say: You go back up the passage and stand in the gateway. The iron has kept its own cold and gives you none of yours back.

objects.name: the way back to the gate

gate.line: The path ends at iron. The hill has been cut open and shut again.

open.say: The gate stands where you left it, swung in. The cold coming through it is older than the cold on this side.
The key turns once, hard, and something in the iron lets go. The gate swings in as far as the hinges will carry it. The key stays in the slot, and you leave it there.

open.refuse: The gate does not move. The keyway is a slot the length of your finger, cut for a key you are not carrying.

search.say: He went down sitting and stayed sitting. The straps are still over his shoulders and the pack under them is empty. In the fold of his belt is a key, rusted through at the ring and whole where it has to be.
There is nothing more on him. His hands are turned up and open.

objects.name: a bearer, sat against the stone

read.say: The mark from the stone runs all through it, and once you hold one mark the rest come loose. It is a procession. Every figure walks to the water carrying something, and walks out of it carrying nothing. The line cut under them is a price, and the price is the crossing itself: what you pay to come over is the memory of coming over.
The procession runs the way it ran before. The wall has said its one thing.
The carving goes from the floor to above your head. Figures in a line, and marks between them that will not hold still long enough to be marks.

objects.name: a mural cut into the wall

follow.say: You step through into the hill. The cut goes on past the iron, squared and floored, and it goes down.

follow.refuse: The gate is shut across the way on, wall to wall, and there is no going round iron.

objects.name: the way on, past the gate

shore.line: Grey water, and no far side to it.

study.say: The stone is warm where nothing else is. A mark is cut into the top of it, deep enough to read with your thumb.

read.say: The marks hold still. They are names in a line, all walking the same way.

read.refuse: The marks swim. You cannot hold them.

objects.name: a book, face up in the shingle

look.say: The pool is shallow and clear. Your face does not arrive in it.

listen.say: You hold still and listen. There is your breath, and the water, and nothing under either.

follow.say: The path climbs off the shingle and inland. It runs the way the names run in the book.

follow.refuse: The path goes up into the dark. You have no name for what is at the top of it.
